title: Ecclesiastical History of the English Nation
author: Bede the Venerable
source: Translated by Claude from stoa0054.stoa006.perseus-lat1, as held by the Perseus Digital Library.

passages.original: quibus sanctus Augustinus, sicut et ceteri patres orthodoxi, multis sententiarum catholicarum milibus responderunt, nec eorum tamen dementiam corrigere ualebant; sed, quod grauius est, correpta eorum uesania magis augescere contradicendo, quam fauendo ueritati uoluit emundari. Quod pulchre uersibus heroicis Prosper rethor insinuat, cum ait:
passages.english: To these men Saint Augustine, like the other orthodox fathers as well, replied with many thousands of catholic arguments, and yet they were not able to correct their madness; but, what is more serious, their frenzy, once rebuked, chose to grow greater by contradicting rather than to be cleansed by assenting to the truth. This the rhetorician Prosper elegantly conveys in heroic verse, when he says:
passages.notes: "sententiarum catholicarum" may mean "catholic statements/opinions" or "authoritative judgements"; rendered "arguments".

passages.original: MISIT etiam tunc isdem uenerandus pontifex ad Etherium Arelatensem archiepiscopum, ut Augustinum Brittaniam pergentem benigne susciperet, litteras, quarum iste est textus:
passages.english: At that time the same venerable pontiff also sent a letter to Etherius, archbishop of Arles, asking him to receive Augustine kindly as he travelled to Britain; its text is as follows:
passages.notes: "Etherius" (Aetherius) was in fact bishop of Lyons; the attribution to Arles is the text's own.

passages.original: II. Interrogatio Augustini: Cum una sit fides, sunt ecclesiarum diuersae consuetudines, et altera consuetudo missarum in sancta Romana ecclesia, atque altera in Galliarum tenetur?
passages.english: II. Augustine's question: Since the faith is one, why are there different customs among the churches, with one custom of masses observed in the holy Roman church and another in the churches of the Gauls?

passages.original: III. Interrogatio Augustini: Obsecro, quid pati debeat, siquis aliquid de ecclesia furtu abstulerit?
passages.english: III. Augustine's question: I beg [you to tell me], what punishment ought someone to suffer if he has taken anything away from a church by theft?

passages.original: IIII. Interrogatio Augustini: Si debeant duo germani fratres singulas sorores accipere, quae sunt ab illis longa progenie generatae?
passages.english: IV. Augustine's question: Whether two full brothers may each marry a sister, [the sisters] being descended from them by a distant line of kinship?

passages.original: V. Interrogatio Augustini: Usque ad quotam generationem fideles debeant cum propinquis sibi coniugio copulari? et nouercis et cognatis si liceat copulari coniugio?
passages.english: V. Augustine's question: To what generation may the faithful be joined in marriage with their relatives? And is it lawful to be joined in marriage with stepmothers and with kinswomen [by marriage]?
passages.notes: "cognatis" here probably means relatives by marriage (e.g. a brother's wife), as Gregory's answer suggests.

passages.original: VI. Interrogatio Augustini: Si longinquitas itineris magna interiacet, ut episcopi non facile ualeant conuenire, an debeat sine aliorum episcoporum praesentia episcopus ordinari?
passages.english: VI. Augustine's question: If a great length of journey lies between [them], so that bishops cannot easily come together, may a bishop be ordained without other bishops being present?

passages.original: VII. Interrogatio Augustini: Qualiter debemus cum Galliarum atque Brittaniarum episcopis agere?
passages.english: VII. Augustine's question: How ought we to deal with the bishops of the Gauls and of the Britains?

passages.original: VIII. Interrogatio Augustini: Si pregnans mulier debeat baptizari? aut postquam genuerit, post quantum tempus possit ecclesiam intrare? aut etiam, ne morte praeoccupetur, quod genuerit, post quot dies hcc liceat sacri baptismatis sacramenta percipere?
passages.english: VIII. Augustine's question: Whether a pregnant woman ought to be baptized? Or, after she has given birth, after how long a time may she enter the church? Or also, so that it may not be overtaken by death, after how many days may what she has borne lawfully receive the sacrament of holy baptism?
passages.notes: "hcc" is a scanning error, apparently for "hoc" (referring to the child); translated accordingly.

passages.original: VIIII. Interrogatio Augustini: Si post inlusionem, quae per somnium solet accedere, uel corpus Domini quislibet accipere ualeat: uel, si sacerdos sit, sacra mysteria celebrare?
passages.english: IX. Augustine's question: Whether, after the illusion that tends to come in a dream, anyone may receive the body of the Lord; or, if he is a priest, celebrate the holy mysteries?

passages.original: HUCUSQUE responsiones beati papae Gregorii ad consulta reuerentissimi antistitis Augustini. Epistulam uero, quam se Arelatensi episcopo fecisse commemorat, ad Uergilium Aetherii successorem dederat; cuius haec forma est:
passages.english: Thus far the answers of the blessed Pope Gregory to the inquiries of the most reverend bishop Augustine. The letter, however, which he mentions he had written to the bishop of Arles, he had addressed to Vergilius, the successor of Aetherius; its form is as follows:

passages.original: Ut idem Augustino pallium et epistulam et plures uerbi ministros miserit.
passages.english: How the same [pope] sent Augustine the pallium, a letter, and more ministers of the word.

passages.original: Ut Augustinum per litteras, ne de uirtutibus suis gloriaretur, hortatus sit.
passages.english: How he exhorted Augustine by letter not to glory in his miracles.
passages.notes: Chapter heading. 'Virtutibus' here means miracles (works of power).

passages.original: Ut Augustinus ecclesiam Saluatoris instaurauerit, et monasterium beati Petri apostoli fecerit; et de primo eius abbate Petro.
passages.english: How Augustine restored the church of the Saviour and built the monastery of the blessed apostle Peter; and concerning its first abbot, Peter.

passages.original: Primam quoque et ultimam Ezechielis prophetae partem, quae uidebantur obscuriores, per omelias XX et duas, quantum lucis intus habeant, demonstrauit. Excepto libello responsionum, quem ad interrogationes sancti Augustini primi Anglorum gentis episcopi scripsit, ut et supra docuimus, totum ipsum libellum his inserentes historiis; libello quoque synodico, quem cum episcopis Italiae de necessariis ecclesiae causis utillimum conposuit, et familiaribus ad quosdam litteris.
passages.english: He also showed, in twenty-two homilies, how much light is contained within the first and last parts of the prophet Ezekiel, which seemed more obscure. [This is] besides the little book of answers which he wrote to the questions of Saint Augustine, first bishop of the English nation, as we have also shown above, inserting that whole little book into this history; and the synodal book, a most useful work, which he composed with the bishops of Italy concerning the necessary affairs of the Church; and letters to certain persons of his acquaintance.
passages.notes: The second sentence is elliptical (ablative absolutes depending on the preceding list of works); 'besides' supplies the sense.

passages.original: Quia enim perceptis caelestibus uerbis, clarescentibus quoque miraculis, uirtus ei diuinae cognitionis infunditur, eiusdem diuinitatis terrore refrenatur, ut praue agere metuat, ac totis desideriis ad aeternitatis gratiam uenire concupiscat. Quibus uerbis beatus Gregorius hoc quoque declarat, quia sanctus Augustinus et socii eius non sola praedicatione uerborum, sed etiam caelestium ostensione signorum gentem Anglorum ad agnitionem ueritatis perducebant.
passages.english: For because, having received the heavenly words, and with miracles also shining forth, the power of the knowledge of God is poured into him, he is restrained by the dread of that same Godhead, so that he fears to act wickedly and longs with all his desires to come to the grace of eternity. By these words blessed Gregory also declares this: that Saint Augustine and his companions were leading the English nation to the knowledge of the truth not by the preaching of words alone, but also by the display of heavenly signs.
passages.notes: The subject of the first sentence ('him') is the converted people/ocean of Britain from the quoted passage of Gregory's Moralia on Job.

passages.original: Ut Augustinus Brettonum episcopos pro pace catholica, etiam miraculo caelesti coram eis facto, monuerit; quaeue illos spernentes ultio secuta sit.
passages.english: How Augustine admonished the bishops of the Britons for the sake of catholic peace, even performing a heavenly miracle in their presence; and what vengeance followed them when they spurned [him].

passages.original: qui tamen et ipsi ad curam episcopi familiariter pertinerent. Quia nimirum Aidan, qui primus eius loci episcopus fuit, cum monachis illuc et ipse monachus adueniens monachicam in eo conuersationem instituit; quomodo et prius beatus pater Augustinus in Cantia fecisse noscitur, scribente ei reuerentissimo papa Gregorio, quod et supra posuimus. Sed quia tua fraternitas, inquit, monasterii regulis erudita seorsum fieri non debet a clericis suis, in ecclesia Anglorum, quae nuper auctore Deo ad fidem perducta est, hanc debet conuersationem instituere, quae initio nascentis ecclesiae fuit patribus nostris;
passages.english: who nevertheless themselves also belonged as members of his household to the bishop's charge. For indeed Aidan, who was the first bishop of that place, coming there as a monk himself with monks, established the monastic way of life in it; just as the blessed father Augustine is known to have done earlier in Kent, when the most reverend Pope Gregory wrote to him, as we have also set down above: 'But since your Fraternity,' he says, 'trained in the rules of a monastery, ought not to live apart from your clergy, you ought to establish in the church of the English, which has lately by God's doing been brought to the faith, that way of life which existed among our fathers at the beginning of the infant Church;
passages.notes: The passage begins mid-sentence; the antecedent of 'who' is the monks/clergy at Lindisfarne mentioned in the preceding context.
